<script type="module" src="https://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/model-viewer/3.4.0/model-viewer.min.js"></script>

Here we view different geometric structures on a torus.  We use color to represent the **metric distortion** — how much the surface area of small neighborhoods differs from the initial torus (R=10, r=3). The color mapping uses coolwarm centered at 1.0. This means if a face has the same area as the baseline, it will appear grey/white. If it's larger, it turns red; if smaller, it turns blue. 

The image projected onto the torus is stretched in some places and compressed in others.  The colors on the right torus indicate this distortion.


::: {layout="[50, 50]" layout-valign="top"}

    id="torus-scrubber-1"

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

# 1. Load the files
# this was created in tt_compute_stats.r
combined_payload = read_csv("assets/torus_grid_sweep/combined_payload.csv")

# 4. Inject into JS
stats_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(combined_payload)
cat(paste0("<script>var frameStats = ", stats_json, ";</script>"))
```
<script>
    function updateVisualization() {
        // These now get an integer index (0-30)
        const i = parseInt(document.querySelector('#slider-R').value);
        const j = parseInt(document.querySelector('#slider-r').value);
        
        // These are just for display purposes, showing the actual radius values from the manifest
        const displayR = document.querySelector('#val-R');
        const displaySmallR = document.querySelector('#val-r');

        // Ensure this matches the number of 'r' steps in your Python sweep
        const RESOLUTION = 31; 
        const idx = (i * RESOLUTION) + j;
        const currentData = frameStats[idx];
    
        if (currentData) {
            const viewer1 = document.querySelector('#torus-scrubber-1');
            const viewer2 = document.querySelector('#torus-scrubber-2');
            
            viewer1.src = `assets/tt/texture_torus_R${i}_r${j}.glb`;
            viewer2.src = `assets/tt30/R${i}_r${j}.glb`;
    
            // This pulls the actual radius (e.g., 5.0, 15.0) from the manifest
            document.querySelector('#val-R').innerText = currentData.r_major.toFixed(2);
            document.querySelector('#val-r').innerText = currentData.r_minor.toFixed(2);
    
            document.querySelector('#max-val').innerText  = currentData.max.toFixed(3);
            document.querySelector('#mean-val').innerText = currentData.mean.toFixed(3);
            document.querySelector('#min-val').innerText  = currentData.min.toFixed(3);
        }
    }

    const sR = document.querySelector('#slider-R');
    const sr = document.querySelector('#slider-r');

    // Just ensure they match your actual data resolution
    sR.addEventListener('input', updateVisualization);
    sr.addEventListener('input', updateVisualization);
    window.addEventListener('load', updateVisualization);
</script>
